about: Difficulty 1-10 (Dom 2026-10-27: the level-18 Pitborn/Minotaur beats the player ~70 % of fights; 'a data layer for easy toggling, and game balance matching later once we introduce the online and MMO element'). A difficulty row is a THIN OVERRIDE LAYER on an opponent profile row (data/profiles.json, the donor pattern of AzerothCore creature_template + creature_template_difficulty and EQEmu npc_types: the profile is the creature, the difficulty row only overrides its knobs and scales). A row overrides exactly two things: the nine brain knobs (the V1 AiProfile names of data/brains.json: reaction = ticks before a fresh swing is noticed; accuracy = timing precision; parry / dodge = chance a noticed swing is parried / rolled; aggression = attack cadence; pressure = share of non-punish attacks that are lights; discipline = stamina floor (% of the bar) under which he backs off; lapse = chance a noticed swing gets no answer; read = chance he guards the side the swing comes from) laid over the profile's brain, and foeHealthScale / foeDamageScale (multipliers on the opponent's health bar, and on every blow and special he lands; src/difficulty.ts). The fight config the sim is built from is the PAIR { profile id, difficulty row id }: plain data, deterministic (no RNG, no clock), so a server can pick the row per encounter and replay the same fight; Gate 0 (the 60 Hz sim) sees only the bodies and profiles it is handed and does not read this file. PvP rows would not use it: a PvP fighter is a player's own sheet and build, never a creature row, so there is no profile and no difficulty row on either side. Ladder 1-10 only for now; later columns (the hero's level, a gear score) join a row the same way: a new key in the row, a new key in the schema (src/sim/validate.js), a new range check, nothing in the sim. THE LADDER (documented, monotonic): 1 is very forgiving (he notices a swing 60 ticks late, answers it a fifth of the time, almost never guards or rolls, and has half the health and hits for half), 10 is V1's level-18 Pitborn untouched (his V1 knobs from moves-tables-defs.json at level 18, scales 1: the same fight as ?ai=v1). Rows 2-9 are the straight line between them (each knob rounded: ticks and stamina to whole numbers, the rest to 2 decimals), so every knob moves one way with the number (reaction and discipline and lapse fall, everything else rises) and a test pins that. `legacy` is the named row for the fight V3 played before this setting existed (data/brains.json novice brain, scales 1); ?difficulty=legacy plays it exactly. `default` names the row a page plays with no ?difficulty= (see the PR for why that row and the measured win rate of each). ?difficulty=N picks a row; an unknown or out-of-range value plays the default and logs a console warning (never throws). ?ai=v1 still plays V1's AI profile untouched, whatever the row (the scales still apply).
